lines.text: In Cairo, Egypt's president, Gamal Abdel Nasser, closed the Straits of Tiran to Israeli ships.
In Amman, Jordan's King Hussein made his choice. He flew to Cairo.
In Israel, the new defence minister, Moshe Dayan, wanted to strike first.
On the twenty-second of May, Egypt closed the straits. On the fifth of June, Israel struck first. On the seventh, the Old City of Jerusalem fell. And on the tenth, the guns went quiet.

On the twenty-second of May, Egypt closed the straits. For two weeks, the world held its breath. Then, at seven forty-five on the morning of the fifth of June, Israeli jets crossed into Egypt. On the seventh, the Old City of Jerusalem fell. And on the tenth, the guns went quiet.
